title: Extract exact ideal Bell pairs from a driven-dephasing bath
statement: An explicit valid environmental filter and local weight-one selection attain the cubic-log order in the qubit specialization.

evidence.quote: ## 4. The strongest direct implementation uses logarithmic memory

requires: Fix finite dimension d and a time-independent Lindblad generator L(rho)=-i[H,rho]+sum_a(L_a rho L_a^dagger-{L_a^dagger L_a,rho}/2), using a canonical TRACELESS Lindblad family and its associated Hamiltonian. N_t=exp(tL); B_t=N_t^c is the FULL PURE-ENVIRONMENT coherent complementary channel. Alice prepares inputs and may retain a reference; Bob receives the complete coherent environmental output; residual source is discarded. Each use has a fresh environment. LOCC and two-way classical communication are available, with NO initial shared entanglement. Q_two-way is qubits per fresh use. Generator/dimension stay fixed as t decreases; a fixed time unit makes log(1/t) dimensionless. Exact rational-complex/algebraic descriptions support the stated branch tests; physical coefficient/interface acquisition is separate.
Driven dephasing L(rho)=-i[Omega X/2,rho]+gamma(Z rho Z-rho),gamma>0,Omega!=0; known input/output rotations and complete coherent four-dimensional effective environment labeled I,X,Y,Z.
provides: Pauli probabilities qI=(1-alpha)(1-beta),qZ=alpha(1-beta),qY=(1-alpha)beta,qX=alpha beta, with alpha=gamma*t+O(t^2), beta=gamma*Omega^2*t^3/12+O(t^5). Let u=(sqrt(qZ)|I>+sqrt(qI)|Z>)/sqrt(qI+qZ); F=|0><u|+i|1><Y| is contractive because selected input vectors are orthonormal.

For a locally prepared source/reference Bell pair, define A0=4qI qZ/(qI+qZ),s=(A0+2qY)/2,A=A0/(A0+2qY),B=qY/(A0+2qY). Success probability is s; normalized state is |psi><psi|+B|01><01| with psi=sqrt(A)|00>+sqrt(B)|11>,A+2B=1, and exactly absent|10> population.

On m independent successful primitive states, local Hamming-weight-one projections reject every|01> noise factor. Unnormalized output is m B A^(m-1) Phi_m; q_m=m B A^(m-1). For m=2^r, acceptance gives exactly r ideal Bell pairs. Taking m=Theta(B^-1)=Theta(t^-2) makes q_m bounded below.

Yield per ORIGINAL source use is R_m=(qY/2)*A^(m-1)*log2(m)=Theta(t^3 log(1/t)), retaining primitive failures. Fixed two-rail extraction yields onlyTheta(t^3). Matching adaptive upper bound is h2(beta); leading lower/upper constants are not asserted equal.
